Argentina won the 2022 World Cup in Lusail, defeating France on penalties after an astonishing 3-3 draw in one of the greatest finals in football history. Lionel Messi scored twice and Angel Di Maria added a brilliant team goal as Argentina dominated the first hour of the match with high pressing and fluid movement in midfield.

France looked lethargic until Kylian Mbappé scored twice in 97 seconds late in the second half to force extra time. Mbappé completed his hat-trick with a late penalty after Messi had restored Argentina's lead in extra time. Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez made a crucial last-second save from Randal Kolo Muani before saving Kingsley Coman's penalty in the shootout.

Tactically, Lionel Scaloni surprised France by starting Angel Di Maria on the left wing. Di Maria targeted Jules Koundé and Ousmane Dembélé, winning a penalty for Messi's opener and scoring the second after a swift five-pass counter-attack involving Alexis Mac Allister and Julian Alvarez. Didier Deschamps made double substitutions before half-time, replacing Giroud and Dembélé to switch to a direct 4-2-4 system.

The victory capped Lionel Messi's international career with the missing trophy, giving Argentina their third World Cup title and first since 1986. Scaloni's tactical flexibility and middle-block pressing scheme contained Antoine Griezmann's playmaker influence throughout the opening 75 minutes.
